Before you sign a buyer agreement, read this. 1) In Ontario it must be in writing and presented to you as soon as possible. 2) The expiry date must be on the first page. 3) Know the fee and when it can change. 4) Check the holdover clause: how long fees may apply after it ends. 5) Ask what services are included and how the agreement can end. (Source: RECO, Signing a contract with a real estate brokerage.)

Renting in Cambridge? Do this math first. Put your rent next to the full monthly cost of owning: mortgage, property tax, home insurance, utilities, repairs and condo fees if any. Then add the upfront costs: down payment and closing costs.

4 budget mistakes first-time buyers make in Ontario. 1) Saving only for the down payment; closing costs come too. 2) Forgetting ongoing costs: property tax, insurance, utilities and repairs. 3) Spending up to your pre-approval limit instead of your comfort level. 4) Not checking whether you could afford a higher rate at renewal. Send this to someone buying their first home.
